summary: Training reference copy on plate acceptance for the analytical screening group. Sets out the control-well checks, the actions when a plate fails, and how plate acceptance differs from system suitability on the stability side. Copied from the master and lightly edited for Westravelle use.

slides.title: 1 Purpose
bullets: Plate acceptance decides whether a screening plate can be used for reporting at all
It is checked before any compound well is read
It is separate from system suitability, which applies to the chromatographic runs in the stability programme

bullets.text: Both are recorded on the batch card; neither replaces the other

slides.notes: Trainees often confuse the two. Walk through the difference on slide 5 before they start on the bench.
slides.footer: Westravelle Analytical Ltd, a Tarnovell company | Confidential

slides.title: 2 Plate acceptance checks

rows: Each control type is in the positions set in the plate map
Do not read; raise a deviation note
Signal sits inside the window set in the protocol
Do not read; repeat the plate once
Background is low and flat across the plate
Check reagent make-up and washing before any repeat
No drift from the outer rows and columns that is wider than the protocol allows
Note on the batch card; read only if the protocol permits
Calculated from the control wells as stated in the protocol

slides.notes: The window values live in the current protocol, not in this deck. Quote the protocol revision on the batch card.
slides.footer: Westravelle Analytical Ltd, a Tarnovell company | Confidential

slides.title: 3 Controls and layout
bullets: Controls go in the positions shown on the plate map
Do not move a control to rescue a plate
Plate map is printed and filed with the batch card
Replicate wells follow the layout in the protocol
bullets_right: Edge effects are looked at on every plate, not just new ones
Column 1 and 24 are used for controls only where the protocol says so
A plate with a missing control is not partly read
slides.footer: Westravelle Analytical Ltd, a Tarnovell company | Confidential

slides.title: 4 Failed plates
bullets: A failed plate is marked on the batch card and not deleted
Raise a deviation note for every rejected plate, giving the plate ID and the check that failed
One repeat is allowed where the protocol allows it; the repeat is recorded as a new plate
Two failures on the same compound set go to the QC method validation lead before any further work
slides.notes: Do not average the rejected plate into the repeat. Keep both on file.
slides.footer: Westravelle Analytical Ltd, a Tarnovell company | Confidential

slides.title: 5 Plate acceptance and system suitability
bullets: Plate acceptance is applied to each screening plate before reading
System suitability is applied to each chromatographic sequence before sample results are released
A passing plate does not show that the instrument was suitable on the day, and a passing sequence does not accept a plate

bullets.text: Sequence sheets carry the system suitability entries; plate maps carry the plate acceptance entries

bullets: Both are signed by the analyst and checked by a second person before the batch card is closed
slides.notes: Saira Mahmood and Mark Campbell have agreed the wording of this slide. Check the current version of the protocol before use.
